question: What is the primary goal of orienting a newly admitted patient to the ward?

options.A: To give the doctor time to finish other ward rounds
options.B: To test the patient's memory and cognitive function
options.C: To reduce anxiety and help them adjust to the new environment
options.D: To ensure the patient fills out their discharge papers early

explanation: A good orientation helps a frightened or stressed patient feel secure by showing them how things work around the ward. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why must a nurse demonstrate the call bell system immediately upon a patient's arrival?

options.A: It distracts the patient from their current physical pain
options.B: It gives the patient a direct way to call for help when needed
options.C: It proves to the visiting family members that the equipment works
options.D: Hospital policy requires it to be tested every single hour

explanation: Showing the patient the call bell ensures they can easily summon assistance for urgent needs like using the toilet or managing sudden pain. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h1)

question: An admission that is planned well in advance for a scheduled surgical procedure is called what?
explanation: Elective admissions are scheduled ahead of time because the patient's condition is stable enough to wait for a convenient date. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h2)

question: A patient arrives at the ward with a large amount of cash and expensive jewelry. What should the nurse do first regarding these valuables?

options.A: Tell the patient to wear the jewelry so nobody can steal it
options.B: Lock the cash inside the bedside table drawer and keep the key
options.C: Place the items in the open utility room for safe keeping
options.D: Follow hospital policy to document and secure the items safely

explanation: Valuables must be documented on an inventory list and stored securely according to hospital protocol, preferably sent home with family or locked in the main safe. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which piece of information is most critical to document immediately during a patient's admission assessment?
explanation: Documenting allergies immediately prevents the accidental administration of medications that could cause severe or life-threatening reactions. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is it important to complete admission documentation promptly rather than waiting until the end of a long shift?

options.A: So that nurses can leave work before their shift officially ends
options.B: To allow the patient to take the paper home immediately
options.C: Because ward managers check handwriting speeds daily
options.D: To prevent forgetting important clinical details and ensure safety

explanation: Writing down observations immediately ensures accuracy and provides oncoming staff with up-to-date information for safe care delivery. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for initiating a patient referral to another facility?

options.A: The hospital building needs routine plumbing repairs
options.B: The patient's clinical needs exceed current facility resources
options.C: The attending doctor wants to take a short vacation
options.D: The patient complains about the food quality on the ward

explanation: Referrals are done when specialized care, advanced equipment, or specific expertise is required that the current health center cannot provide. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h4)

question: Before physically transporting a patient for an external referral, what crucial step must the nurse or doctor complete?

options.A: Contact the receiving facility to confirm bed availability and acceptance
options.B: Ask the patient to pay all hospital bills in full cash
options.C: Throw away all previous paper records to save luggage space
options.D: Wait for the patient's extended family to arrive from another city

explanation: Checking in advance ensures the receiving hospital is ready and expecting the patient, avoiding dangerous delays in ongoing treatment. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h4)

question: What term describes moving a patient from the surgical ward to the operating theatre within the same hospital?
explanation: An intra-facility transfer refers to moving a patient between different units or departments inside the same hospital building or compound. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h5)

question: A critically ill patient on oxygen support needs to be transferred to the CT scan room. Who is best suited to accompany this patient?

options.A: A qualified nurse or doctor with portable oxygen and emergency gear
options.B: An administrative clerk who knows the shortcut hallways well
options.C: The patient's visiting relative who agreed to watch the monitor
options.D: A hospital security guard who can help push the wheeled trolley

explanation: Unstable or critically ill patients must always be escorted by trained clinical staff equipped to handle sudden emergencies during transit. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h5)

question: At what point in the patient's hospital stay should discharge planning ideally begin?
explanation: Discharge planning starts early so the care team has enough time to arrange equipment, home support, and education before the patient leaves. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why is family involvement important during the discharge planning process?

options.A: Relatives need to drive the nursing staff home after their shift ends
options.B: Family members often provide ongoing care and support at home
options.C: Family members must clean the hospital bed before the next patient arrives
options.D: Relatives are legally required to sign the hospital utility bills

explanation: Involving family ensures that the people assisting the patient at home understand medication routines, warning signs, and necessary lifestyle changes. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the proper nursing action when a competent patient insists on leaving the hospital before treatment is complete?

options.A: Explain the risks and have them sign a discharge against medical advice form
options.B: Ignore the request and refuse to give them their personal clothes
options.C: Call the police immediately to physically lock the patient inside the room
options.D: Hide the patient's shoes so they cannot walk out of the ward

explanation: A competent adult has the right to leave, but the nurse must warn them of potential dangers and document the event by having them sign a DAMA form. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing responsibility during a routine patient discharge?

options.A: Documenting the exact time and manner of the patient's departure
options.B: Ordering new hospital beds for the entire ward
options.C: Explaining home medication schedules and follow-up dates
options.D: Returning patient valuables that were kept in safe custody

explanation: Ordering new beds is an administrative task unrelated to the direct responsibilities involved in discharging an individual patient. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h7)
